title: Act III, Scene I
focus: 'To be, or not to be' and the nunnery scene

teacherSummary.text: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern report failure. Claudius and Polonius hide to watch Hamlet with Ophelia. Hamlet meditates on life, death and action. Ophelia returns his gifts; he denies loving her, tells her to go to a nunnery, and rails against marriage. Claudius decides to send Hamlet to England.

criticalVoices.quote: Hence we see a great, an almost enormous, intellectual activity, and a proportionate aversion to real action consequent upon it, with all its symptoms and accompanying qualities. This character Shakspeare places in circumstances, under which it is obliged to act on the spur of the moment:--Hamlet is brave and careless of death; but he vacillates from sensibility, and procrastinates from thought, and loses the power of action in the energy of resolve.
